title: Range on a timestamp: every new write lands on the last shard
caption: New rows always carry the largest key, so the newest range takes all of today's writes while older shards sit idle.

steps.text: Orders are keyed by created_at and each shard owns a range of months.
Every insert has created_at = now, which falls in the newest range: one node takes 100% of write traffic.
Older shards only serve occasional reads of history. Three shards, the write capacity of one.
Fix: hash the key, or lead with a well-spread column such as (customer_id, created_at), so writes spread while one customer's orders stay sorted.
